conditions: on AC Power, 1-min load average before each run 6.2 median / 6.7 max

contenders.sillon: @sillon/react parts over streamPeaks(): fetch-streamed MP3, WebCodecs decode in a worker, 256-sample max-abs peaks; plus a preload=metadata <audio> as usePlayer creates.
contenders.sillon-fallback: sillon with its worker forced to report unsupported: whole-file fetch + OfflineAudioContext.decodeAudioData at 44.1 kHz, peaks on the main thread.
contenders.ws: wavesurfer.js 8.0.2 defaults (url only): fetch + decodeAudioData into an 8 kHz AudioContext.
contenders.ws-peaks: wavesurfer.js 8.0.2 with precomputed 8000-point peaks JSON + duration (its long-file advice); JSON fetch timed, server step in serverPeaksCost.
contenders.naive: fetch + new AudioContext().decodeAudioData + per-pixel max on the main thread + canvas.
contenders.peaksjs: peaks.js 4.0.0 overview with precomputed data in the layout `audiowaveform -b 8` writes (256 samples per pixel, channels averaged), made here from ffmpeg; the .dat fetch is timed, served uncompressed.
contenders.peaksjs-webaudio: peaks.js 4.0.0 overview with its Web Audio path: XHR for the whole file, decodeAudioData, waveform data on the main thread.

notes.feed: 20 waveforms of 20 different 3-minute speech files (CBR 128 kbps) on one page, each with something that can play it. sillon: one useAudio() per item with library defaults (each waveform draws once its file is read; all 20 stream at once). wavesurfer.js: one WaveSurfer.create per item (defaults, or precomputed peaks). peaks.js: one overview per item (precomputed .dat, or Web Audio with one shared AudioContext). "Complete" is when the last of the 20 is on screen.
runtime: Both libraries draw the same 1-hour file from the same precomputed data (ffmpeg, 256-sample max-abs), so nothing is decoded during the test. 1200 px wide, 2 px bars, 1 px gaps.

Each scenario runs 8 s: playback (the audio plays, muted; played part and cursor follow it), zoom (the view sweeps from the whole hour to 5 s at 30:00 and back, set every frame), resize (container width swings 600–1200 px every frame).

Main-thread time is Chromium's Performance.getMetrics TaskDuration (plus its script, layout and style parts), in ms per second of wall time, unthrottled only: under CDP CPU throttling those counters went down for light work (bench/metrics-check.mjs), so throttled runs report frame timing only.
CPU throttling (CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate) slows the page's main thread only. That is fine here, since neither library uses a worker after loading.

Slow frames: share of animation frames longer than 1.5× the median frame. Redraws: sillon, changes to its clip path; wavesurfer.js, its redrawcomplete events. Commits: React commits during the window, counted through the React DevTools hook.
wavesurfer.js waits for resizing to pause (100 ms) before redrawing, so during a continuous resize it does less work and shows its old drawing stretched; sillon redraws every frame.
notes.memory: Peak memory: most RSS of the browser's whole process tree while loading, minus the same tree idle on a blank page. Memory while open: the same, measured 3 s after loading finished plus 1 s after a forced garbage collection (Chromium only). RSS is what the OS has handed the browser; memory freed inside the browser is not always returned right away, so "while open" can include memory the page no longer uses.
method: Fresh browser process per run, cold cache, seeded-random interleaved order, 1 s pause between runs.
Times are ms since navigation start (bundle load counts). Drawn = second rAF after the first draw with real data.
Network shaped at the server with one shared token bucket (DevTools emulation may skip worker fetches). JS/HTML/JSON gzipped.
Memory: RSS of the whole browser process tree sampled every 100 ms, minus the same tree idle on a blank page.
CPU: CPU seconds of that tree from navigation to complete, all threads. TBT: Chromium long tasks only.
Accuracy: vs ffmpeg decode (gapless-trimmed), ~20 000 bins aligned to 256-sample reference buckets.
sillon bundle includes React + ReactDOM (~65 kB gz), counted against it. JS transferred: every JavaScript response as served (gzipped), worker scripts included.
caveats: One machine, headless browsers, on AC Power, 1-min load average before each run 6.2 median / 6.7 max; absolute numbers will differ elsewhere.
Speech corpus (TTS); wavesurfer decodes at 8 kHz by default, so its peak accuracy is lower by design and the difference is invisible at overview zoom.
sillon "first bars" is the start of a left-to-right stream, not the whole waveform; compare "complete" or "half" for the full shape.
Load suites are not CPU-throttled: Chromium's throttling does not reach workers (bench/throttle-check.mjs), so a throttled run would slow the others' decoding but not sillon's.
Music is one 2-minute file (m2m, 192 kbps); the rest of the corpus is speech.
